subject: general
question: The position of the image produced by a concave mirror when an object is placed at a distance such that light rays from the object are parallel to the principal axis is:

options.text: at a point between the principal focus and pole
at the position of the object itself
at a point between the principal focus and the centre of curvature

solution:
The correct answer is __**The principal focus**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When light rays from an object are parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror, they converge after reflection and meet at the **principal focus**.
 
• This is a fundamental property of concave mirrors:
 
• **Parallel rays** to the principal axis always converge at the **focus** after reflection.
 
• Thus, the image will be formed at the principal focus, and it will be **real, inverted**, and highly diminished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae288c9dcb7001f9330e6c4830e1fdce6de95827bc06b2d6f615097a2a2bae90.png] 

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Spherical mirrors are of two types -

 
 
• Convex mirror, and
 
• Concave mirror.
 
 
 
• The image formed by the spherical mirrors depends on the position of the object.

 
• Convex mirror: If the outer surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface then it is called a convex mirror. It is also called the diverging mirror.

 
 
• The nature of the image formed by a convex mirror does not depend on the distance of the object from the mirror. These images are always virtual, smaller than the object, and situated behind the mirror.
 
 
 
• Concave mirror: If the inner surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface, then it is called a concave mirror. It is also called a focusing mirror/converging mirror.
 
 
• The size of the image produced by these mirrors can be larger or smaller than the object, depending upon the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• The concave mirror can form both real as well as virtual images of any object.
 
 
 
• Plane mirrors are the most commonly used mirrors. Lateral inversion is seen in the plane mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
